domain: Destructive batch git operations at real scale, and live multi-host configuration/packaging state verified read-only over SSH
axioms: A precondition checked once at the start of a long, multi-step destructive operation only protects the steps that run before anything could invalidate it; every later step needs either re-verification or an explicit argument for why nothing could have changed.

Git does not preserve meaningful mtimes across checkout/pull/rebase; any staleness check built on filesystem mtime for git-tracked files needs an explicit argument for why that doesn't produce false negatives, not just false positives.

'Checked live on <date>' is a claim about the past; a review of a plan that will execute later must re-verify anything the plan's safety argument depends on, not cite the same snapshot as if it were still true.

A deletion with no corresponding commit is invisible to every report and every verify step the plan writes — 'clean status' and 'untracked' are not the same thing, and a filter built for one can be silently defeated by the other.

Two machines' settings/cache state is not guaranteed identical just because the plan issues the same command on both; a step's precondition (a key existing to delete) can be true on one host and false on the other.

At 48 repos and roughly 2,900 files, a corner case with negligible probability per repo has a real expected count across the corpus; 'unlikely' is not the same evaluation at fixture scale (3 files) as at corpus scale.
primitives: git repo state (branch, tracked/untracked, porcelain status)
failure_mode: Whether the harvest package's own internal record-identity/accretion logic is correct — this lens takes Task 9/12's guarantees as given inputs and only checks whether Task 23 relies on more than they promise, not their internal correctness.

Anything not reachable via read-only inspection of the real corpus or a read-only SSH session to zklw — it does not evaluate code paths that only manifest once data/ and harvest/ exist and have actually run.
